title: [finding] `FilterConditionSchema` still PARSES `{ field: [...] }` and `{ field: { $eq: [...] } }`, so a stored dataset or widget filter publishes clean and is refused at query time on every backend
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with a named landing site**: `FieldOperatorsSchema.$eq` and the implicit-equality branch of `FilterConditionSchema` in `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`. Finding class **(c)**: an AI trap.

Found by the `os-dev` round on #19757 (PR #19882, ruling 乙 `5793368540`: an array in the equality slot is refused at the shared comparand-shape face) and filed by the `domain:spec` execution seat 1 (`session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`, seat post #6017). Devs do not open issues. ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading belong to triage. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens

- Re-read by this seat on `origin/main` `1f89ba0d70`: `$eq: z.any().optional()`. The schema door accepts an array there, and in the implicit-equality position.
- After PR #19882, the query path's shared face refuses exactly that shape on every backend (INVALID_FILTER / 400).

⇒ a stored filter typed `FilterConditionSchema` (e.g. `DatasetSchema.filter`, `DashboardWidgetSchema.filter`) that carries it **publishes clean**, and then fails every query that uses it, for a different person, later. This is the schema-door twin of ruling 乙. The ruling's letter covers the compile face only.

## Producer

AI- or code-authored stored filters (dataset, widget, and any other `FilterConditionSchema` carrier). The implementing round measured the parse; the carrier list is its reading, ⛔ not a census this seat ran.

## ⚠️ This narrows an accept set

Refusing the shape at the schema door narrows published authoring schemas and likely owes an ADR-0087 entry. Triage judges whether ruling 乙 already covers it or it needs its own decision.

## Dedupe

MCP issue search, this repo, closed included, at 2026-09-23T14:52Z: `FilterConditionSchema $eq z.any accepts array equality publishes refused at query time` returned 2 hits, both closed, neither this defect (#19087, #16431).
